_about: Enemies inside a skirmish: the domains' wildlife and the heroes (bible section 9; the names are working names until play moves them, the numbers placeholders at the single-digit scale since the stock pass's landing (22 October): HP 2 to 6 for the rank and file, 30 to 40 massive, 12 to 24 heroes, a blow 1 to 6; the elites and the slate's bosses on a guess of 10 November for the refit pass's model (Ryan: "I'd like you to guesstimate some elite and boss tweaks as well"), their blows sized against a shield that refills: a boss 72 at tier one where it was 48 (a core in parts 40, a part 8 to 18, the Vampire Lord 50 since it may rise once) and its blow 10 to 20 where it was 6 to 10, an elite 16 to 60 and its blow 7 to 18; docs/rules.md, docs/measurements.md). hp is a foe's HP, the foes' word (a machine has hull). Enemy damage is static and telegraphed exactly; only the player's rolled faces roll. rank is where they prefer to stand: front foes step up, back foes hold. size 2 is massive and fills both slots of a column, at any tier. tier (1 to 3, one by default) is the rung of its line a unit stands on: a recolour is a base type in a new hue under a new name, its own foe type with its own numbers and a twist (the Goblin Guard and the Goblin Captain on the Goblin), carrying its tier; which units come is the domain's spawn list at the battle's tier (content/factions.json), a boss's escort included, so the field never reads this. elite true marks a foe that leads an elite composition (content/factions.json; the bible's tiers row: a guaranteed mini-boss event a Fracture spawns mid-battle, outside the spawn lists, scaled by the tier as a boss is since 2 November); its menace is its own numbers' like any foe's (ContentDB.menace: the heaviest implemented blow plus a quarter of HP, rounded up, the one weight for the Rupture meter, Anathema and salvage; doubled until 10 November, while an elite's numbers were a rank and file's). wanders true marks the elite any domain's Fracture may send: drawn by chance (ContentDB.WANDER_CHANCE) in place of the domain's next own elite and always once its own are spent, at random among the wanderers not yet sent this battle (3 November, from the same roll); an elite may come again in a later battle, never twice in one. hero marks one of the party: human-sized, the domain's final, dealt from the domain's bench at the campaign's start; a hero is never in a spawn list. promotes names the hero a massive entry is the class change of, its promoted form fought at the finale (bible section 9): the entry holds what the class change adds (size 2, rank front, its armour, its one move more under actions, a move with one of the hero's ids taking that move's place) and everything else, its name included, is its hero's, read as the content loads. armour (default 0) comes off every blow that lands on the foe, flat, never off Burning, Vitriol or a breaching weapon. No foe resists a suppress by nature: Numbed, from a suppress that lands, is the only resistance. aim is the sense a foe's target pick follows, each foe on its own as the round opens: anything (the default, at random, the baseline the numbers are balanced on), and where a foe's threat calls for one, exposed (weighted toward the machine its blows would hurt most), heat (the hottest machine), armed (a machine showing an intact weapon), focus (the rank shares one pick), buffed (the machine carrying the most stacks). A move may carry its own aim. The foes pick in the order they strike and never over-commit: a machine the blows already picked would wreck is passed over while another stands. on_death {summon, count, pair}: destroyed, the foe splits, that many of the named foe stepping up at once under its pack, the first into the slot it fell from and the rest into the nearest empty slots of their rank, any with no room into the pool; with pair (the Gel, count 2) both halves stand as a pair in its own slot, one slot to the formation (an area blow reaching both, a single-target blow one, no mine laid there while either stands); an arrival's round is over (no intent, acting from the next round), and a split goes one deep; on_death {blow} is a last act, landed the moment it falls. parts, guard and regrow_parts make a core in parts. Player-facing text: codex (what the codex says), flavour (an in-world quote), and each action's text. Every move wears the genre's name where the genre has one (Protect, Cure, Fire, Steal, Self-Destruct) while the engine's words stay ours; the plaque announces a named move when it lands (bible section 9). design is internal and never shown: fantasy (the pitch, the source of the homage), niche (the tactical problem the foe poses), sprite and variants (the art's briefs), and notes only where something is still owed. actions is the foe's roster of moves, each kind attack, defend, buff or debuff, with status implemented or planned; only implemented actions appear in the codex, and a planned move may name an effect the engine lacks (interpose, retaliate, regrow_all). Rank and file have one or two moves, a boss or a hero three, the third a signature that opens on a condition. A move may carry when, one word or a list meaning any (below_half, missing_hull, back_behind, others_on_field, ally_hurt, machine_buffed, ally_unready, ally_marked); a move whose condition fails is not rolled, and a special never fires twice running when anything else is open. A defend, buff or debuff names an effect the engine runs (Foe.ACTION_EFFECTS: brace with value (the armour it adds, in stacks of Armoured, a point a stack; brace_all the same on every foe through the next round), regrow with value, regrow_ally (the most hurt of its own); revive_once, revive_once_ally (Reraise on one of its own), summon with foe and count, rally with value; drain_rerolls, burn with value (stacks of Burning on its target), disable, scorch_all with value (stacks of Scorched on every machine), corrupt_all with value (stacks of Corrupted on the entry every machine shows), silence, dispel (Purge); cleanse (every mark the team laid off the most-marked of its own, no value), barrier (a Barrier on itself, no value), regenerate with value (Regenerating on itself), ward_all (a Ward on every foe on the field, no value), prime with value (Primed on every other foe), enrage with value (Enraged: while it stands, every shield, vent or equipment entry the team spends makes its blows value harder for the rest of the fight, a stack a spend; the Goblin Nob's Bellow, 3 November), golden with value and rounds (Golden: a mode, its blows value harder and a point of armour for rounds rounds, 1 to 5 and three unsaid; a quarter of its HP lost since, or a Suppress, breaks it and it staggers out of its next action; the Thunder Ape's Golden Rage, 4 November; its when "calm" holds only while it is not gold)) and is picked by weight like an attack, in place of a blow that turn. A move marked once is used once a fight; one marked opens (with once) is the foe's first move of the fight, taken before any other (the Nob's Bellow). Write {value} in its text for its number. On the map: a foe carries no ring and no hunt, since a composition says whether its pack hunts and a hunter catches at the pounce, one number for every hunter (Ryan, 8 November: "The composition should say if it hunts, not the units"; the rings purged; factions.json's hunts); movespeed in hexes (default 2; foes wade water at two a hex as ground machines do and walls stop them, and a winged foe (winged true) crosses both as a flyer does; bosses patrol 1). An implemented attack scales the base attack: factor (default 1.0), strikes (default 1; each a separate blow), swarm (so much more per other foe of its type on the field), countdown (it gathers that many rounds and lands later), keywords (breach: the blow ignores the shield and the armour, the whole of it reaching the hull; scorch: stacks of Scorched; burn: stacks of Burning; disable and corrupt act on the entry the machine's die shows; crush: stacks of Crushed on the machine, a point more on every blow it takes a stack through the next round; scorch, burn, corrupt and crush each say their stacks a blow beside the keyword, as the player's Burn does ("scorch": 2); self_destruct: the blow spends the striker; all: the blow lands on every machine), weight (default 1; attacks weigh 2 to a special's 1). Write {damage} in an action's text and the resulting number is shown. Foes stand and strike front rank left to right then back rank; the heaviest hitters deploy left. role (a pusher's unless it says hunter or flanker; internal, never shown; Ryan, 9 November: a unit is made for a battlefield role and tuned for the fight that role meets) is what the validator holds a patrol's and a formation's members to: a pusher stands in the formations, a flanker is a duel for one machine in a patrol (the Whisker Cat's, the Roc's, the Dullahan's and Cerberus's lines, 10 November), a hunter leads a pack that hunts (the Dire Wolf's line, the Antlion's); elites, bosses, heroes and parts carry none. Design notes written before 15 November speak of breach and of blows through the shield: the keyword was cut that day (Ryan: "Sure, let's cut breach"), those moves are plain blows that meet the shield and the armour, and the notes wait for the foes' pass.

design.fantasy: The genre's first fight, with a knife. Every JRPG opens on one.
design.niche: The Meadow's front: a straight knife and a scrap shield, a line that holds while the back rank works (Ryan, 10 November: 'A straight attack, and a block of some kind, so they're a true frontliner and not a lame not-really-damage-threat'; 'I think the earlier goblin can have shield wall as well'). Until then its knife counted its peers, 2 and one more for every other goblin standing, and the first kill took the formation apart. The knife's 4 is a placeholder: with the wall it costs two lights about what the old knife did, and any higher out-hits the Guard as it stands.

design.fantasy: The great cat with the long whiskers that stun, the genre's Coeurl under a name of our own (Ryan's bench of 3 November: the Whisker Cat). It prowls the edge of the field alone.
design.niche: Its whiskers switch off the entry the machine is showing as the blow lands, so the question each round they are coming is what to leave showing, and whether to spend the best die first. A flanker: made for a duel with one machine on the flank, never for a formation (Ryan, 9 November: a flanker is a duel, not a small pusher; 10 November: 'Duelists are as you see fit'). Hit points for three or four rounds of one light machine; no armour, which walls the lights whatever else a unit does. Every number a placeholder.

variants: a man-sized green cactus with arms and legs, frozen mid-sprint with one knee raised high and both arms pumping, long needles all over, a menacing face of hollow dark eyes and a thin slit mouth
a man-sized blue-green cactus with arms and legs and a single blood-red flower on its head, frozen in a long leaping stride with one arm thrust forward, needles all over, a menacing face
a man-sized dark green ribbed cactus with arms and legs, frozen low in a sprinter's crouch as if at the start of a race, bristling with needles, a menacing face

a man-sized sun-bleached green cactus with arms and legs, cracked and scarred with broken needles, frozen in a running pose with its body leaning forward and its arms flung back, needles all over, a menacing face

a man-sized green cactus with a ribbed barrel body and stubby arms and legs, frozen stiff in a sprinter's running pose: upright body, legs in a wide stride with one knee lifted, both arms bent sharply at the elbows, one raised high in front and the other swung low behind, rigid as a statue, long needles all over, a face of three dark hollow holes

a burly man-sized dark green cactus with thick ribbed arms and legs, frozen mid-stride in a rigid sprinter's pose: one arm bent up high in front, the other bent down behind, one knee lifted, its body perfectly upright, a menacing face of two dark hollow eyes and a round hollow mouth, needles bristling all over

a man-sized pale green cactus with a single crimson flower on its head, frozen in a stiff running pose with both arms bent at right angles, one up in front and one down behind, its legs split in a long stride, unnaturally still, needles all over, three dark holes for a face

a tall gaunt man-sized cactus, sun-bleached green and scarred, frozen in a sprinter's pose with its elbows bent hard, one fist high in front and one low behind, one leg lifted, a dense halo of long spines, a blank sinister face of dark hollows

a man-sized pale green cactus with a single crimson flower on its head, frozen mid-sprint in an exaggerated running pose: one arm thrust high and far forward, the other swung far back and down, one knee lifted almost to its chest, leaning hard into the stride, bristling with hundreds of long sharp needles, a face of three plain solid black holes

a man-sized pale green cactus with a single crimson flower on its head, long needles fanning out in dense bristling tufts along its arms, back and head, frozen in a deep lunging sprint with both arms bent hard at the elbows, one high in front and one low behind, a face of three plain solid black holes

a man-sized pale green cactus with a single crimson flower on its head, frozen mid-leap in a sprinter's stride with both feet off the ground, its arms bent sharply, one high in front and one low behind, a thick coat of long needles standing straight out all over it, a face of three plain solid black holes

a man-sized pale green cactus with a single crimson flower on its head, its ribbed body studded with rows of long pale needles, frozen in a wide running pose leaning far forward, one arm raised high in front and one swung back behind, its back leg kicked up behind it, a face of three plain solid black holes
design.fantasy: The Cactuar, made sinister: a figure in a running pose that has never been seen to move. Final Fantasy's thousand needles, our fixed needles through anything.
design.niche: Its needles are a fixed number no shield stops, and it comes in fives. Hull and tempo, never the shield.
design.notes: Scatter, a flee, struck 2 November by Ryan's rule: a foe flees only as a loot-runner whose prize goes with it, and the Needler is no such thing.

entries.codex: A cactus the height of a man, in the pose of someone running, and nobody has ever seen one move. Its needles are exactly ten, every time, and a shield does nothing about them.

actions.name: Needles
actions.text: Exactly {damage} needles.

entries.flavour: Appendix K: do not take your eyes off the cactus.

entries.name: Barbed Needler

design.fantasy: The cactuar's barbed cousin: the Waste's theft of entries on the rank and file. Tier two of the needler line.

entries.codex: A needler whose needles stay in. Its blow corrupts the component the machine is showing.

actions.name: Needles
actions.text: Exactly {damage} barbed needles; the one it is showing bites when spent.

entries.flavour: Count the needles. Then count the ones you cannot find.

entries.name: Great Needler

design.fantasy: The giant cactuar and its thousand needles, a countdown. Tier three of the needler line.

entries.codex: The big one. It gathers for two rounds and then looses every needle at once. Kill it, suppress it, or shield what it has picked.

actions.name: Needles
actions.text: Exactly {damage} needles.

actions.name: Thousand Needles
actions.text: Gathers for two rounds, then {damage} needles at once.

entries.flavour: If it starts counting, you have two rounds.

entries.name: Antlion

design.sprite: a giant sand-coloured insect with huge curved mandibles and six spindly legs, crouched low and half buried in a mound of loose sand
variants: a giant sand-coloured insect with huge curved mandibles, rearing up out of a funnel of loose sand with its front legs raised and its mandibles spread wide, six spindly legs
a giant sand-coloured insect with a bloated striped abdomen and huge curved mandibles, lunging forward low on six spindly legs with sand spraying from its feet
a giant sand-coloured insect with a spiked armoured carapace and huge serrated mandibles, dug half into a mound of loose sand with only its head, front legs and jaws thrust out
a giant pale sand-coloured insect with long bristly legs and a flat armoured head, its huge curved mandibles snapping shut, crouched low on six spindly legs and coiled to spring
design.fantasy: The trap at the bottom of the funnel. Final Fantasy's antlion, Dragon Quest's.
design.niche: A hunter of the slowest that pins what it catches and braces when hurt. The slow machine wants company.

entries.codex: Waits under the sand for whatever is slowest and does not let go. Hurt it and it digs in, and what is dug in is hard to hit.

actions.text: Digs in: armour +{value} until its next action.

entries.flavour: The sand moved. Nobody else saw the sand move.

entries.name: Pit Antlion

design.fantasy: The pit's antlion: breach on one more Waste type, and the burrow that is a Barrier. Tier two of the antlion line.

entries.codex: An antlion whose burrow swallows the next blow whole. Pop the barrier with a cheap blow, then hit it.

actions.name: Mandibles
actions.text: Jaws close for {damage}.

actions.name: Burrow
actions.text: Sinks into the sand: the next weapon blow on it deals nothing.

entries.flavour: The sand moved. Then the sand had jaws.

entries.name: Antlion Queen

design.fantasy: The antlion grown to a queen: the Waste's big fixed blow on a countdown. Tier three of the antlion line.

entries.codex: The queen of the pit. Its Devour is announced a round ahead; hurt, it digs in behind three points of plate.

actions.name: Mandibles
actions.text: Jaws close on the hull for {damage}.

actions.name: Devour
actions.text: Rears for a round, then devours: {damage}.

actions.name: Burrow
actions.text: Digs in: armour +{value} until its next action.

entries.flavour: Everything in the badlands is something's lunch. This is the something.

a cockatrice like a giant scaly rooster on clawed lizard legs, mid-charge with its head low and thrust forward and its serpent tail lashing behind
a gaunt stone-grey cockatrice, half bird and half lizard, crouched low and hissing with its wings half spread like a cloak
a cockatrice with iridescent green and gold plumage, leaping forward with its talons raised, its bat wings spread wide and its serpent tail curled

design.niche: Back rank. Stone switches off whatever a machine's die is showing.

entries.name: Basilisk

entries.codex: A cockatrice with an eye for weapons: it aims at a machine showing an intact gun, and its stone switches the gun off.

entries.name: Gorgon

entries.flavour: The Waste takes what you have. This one takes it and leaves it in you.

entries.name: Roc

design.fantasy: The bird that carries off elephants, out of the desert's oldest stories (Ryan's bench of 3 November). Walls and water are nothing to it.
design.niche: It climbs for a round and stoops through the shield, so the question is a Barrier for the stoop, or a kill before it lands. Winged. A flanker: made for a duel with one machine on the flank, never for a formation (Ryan, 9 November: a flanker is a duel, not a small pusher; 10 November: 'Duelists are as you see fit'). Hit points for three or four rounds of one light machine; no armour, which walls the lights whatever else a unit does. Every number a placeholder.

entries.codex: A bird big enough to shade a machine, alone on the flank. Its talons are plain. When it climbs it comes down a round later through any shield: stop that one blow, or finish it first.

actions.name: Talons
actions.text: Talons for {damage}.

actions.text: Climbs for a round, then stoops: {damage}.

entries.flavour: That is not a cloud.

entries.name: Sandworm

design.sprite: a colossal eyeless segmented worm bursting out of the desert sand, its head nothing but a round gaping maw ringed with rows of inward-pointing teeth
variants: a colossal eyeless segmented worm arching up out of the desert sand and curling over to strike down, its head nothing but a round gaping maw ringed with rows of inward-pointing teeth

a colossal eyeless segmented worm with cracked plated segments the colour of sandstone, rising straight up out of the desert sand with sand pouring off it, its head nothing but a round gaping maw ringed with rows of inward-pointing teeth

a colossal eyeless segmented worm with a row of jagged spines down its back, bursting out of the desert sand in a spray of rock and dust, its head nothing but a round gaping maw ringed with rows of inward-pointing teeth thrust forward

a colossal eyeless pale segmented worm with long feeler tendrils around its mouth, rearing up out of the desert sand in a tall curve, its head nothing but a round gaping maw ringed with rows of inward-pointing teeth
design.fantasy: The worm under the desert, the genre's and every desert's. The old Maw's ring of teeth is its mouth.
design.niche: Fills a whole column, bites through the shield, and digs in when hurt. Suppress the maw; hull takes it, a shield does not.
design.notes: A boss stand-in until the slate filled its domain; rank and file since 30 October (Ryan: "they are rank and file after all"), so two moves at tier one, its third (Quake) left for a higher line's twist.

entries.codex: Most of it is under the sand. The part that is not is a ring of teeth the width of a road, and its maw closes hard. Hurt it and it digs in.

actions.text: Digs in: armour +{value} until its next action.

entries.name: Revenant

design.sprite: a skeleton knight in rusted ornate plate armour, an empty helm, torn surcoat, a notched sword
variants: a skeleton knight in rusted plate, lunging forward behind a cracked round shield with its sword arm drawn back, long bony limbs and a small skull set low between hunched armoured shoulders
a skeleton in a tattered royal surcoat over corroded mail, a dented crown on its small skull, leaning forward and reaching out with both long bony hands, its fingers spread like claws

a headless knight in pale bone-white armour striding forward with a cape streaming behind it, holding its own helmeted skull out at arm's length

a skeleton knight in rusted ornate plate armour, an empty helm and a torn surcoat, lunging forward with a notched sword thrust out, long bony limbs and a small helmed head set low between hunched armoured shoulders

a skeleton in rusted scale mail and a horned helm, hunched forward with a rusted axe raised in one bony hand and a broken shield in the other, long bony limbs and a small skull set low between hunched shoulders

a skeleton knight in a rotted priest's vestment over rusted mail, mid-stride and swinging a heavy flanged mace back over its shoulder, long bony limbs and a small skull set low between hunched shoulders

a drowned skeleton knight in corroded green-black plate hung with pond weed, gripping a rusted trident in both bony hands across its body, the shaft held level at its waist, long bony limbs and a small skull set low between hunched armoured shoulders

the same drowned skeleton knight in corroded green-black plate, its rusted trident held across its body in both whole bony hands and forearms, the shaft one straight pole from head to butt
design.fantasy: The dead in rusted ornate plate: a knight's silhouette gone wrong, the helm empty, the plate hanging off the ribs. The genre's zombies and skeletons in one.
design.niche: The Marsh's front: a flat claw and nothing else, the line the ghosts behind it raise again into the gaps a kill opens (Ryan, 10 November: 'Make revenant stab flat, or flat with a Marsh twist, if a simple one exists'; none is simple that is not another unit's already, the rise the Knight's and the Dullahan's, the mend the Wight's, so the twist stays where the Marsh has it, behind and above). Until then its claw counted its peers, 2 and one more for every other revenant standing. The claw's 3 is a placeholder, a step under the goblin's knife since it never stops to block.

entries.codex: The rank and file of the Marsh. Slow, stupid and never alone: six arrive for every one you put down, and they walk straight at the nearest thing with a heartbeat.

actions.name: Claw
actions.text: Tears at anything in reach for {damage}.

entries.flavour: They don't run. They don't have to. You'll get tired first.

entries.name: Wight

design.fantasy: The wight, the Marsh's hard-to-keep-down on the rank and file: Regenerating as a foe's buff. Tier two of the revenant line: the flat claw a step up (4, a placeholder) and the mend its twist.

entries.codex: A revenant that knits itself back together. Hurt, it regrows a little at each action for three rounds: burst it, or purge the mending.

actions.name: Claw
actions.text: Tears at anything in reach for {damage}.

actions.name: Grave Mend
actions.text: Knits itself: regrows {value} at each of its next three actions.

entries.flavour: You can hear it mending. Finish it before it finishes.

entries.name: Draugr

design.fantasy: The draugr, the Marsh's dead at their hardest. Tier three of the revenant line since 10 November (Ryan: 'The tier 3 revenant shouldnt be a lich, it should be, well, a tier 3 revenant'): the revenant's flat claw and the wight's mend at tier three's numbers, no twist of its own. The name is Claude's on his 'Revenant 3 name is whatever you think', for his name pass; its sprite is the Revenant's in a new hue (tools/recolour.py).

entries.codex: A revenant long in the ground and the harder for it. Hurt, it knits faster than a wight: burst it, or purge the mending.

actions.name: Claw
actions.text: Tears at anything in reach for {damage}.

actions.name: Grave Mend
actions.text: Knits itself: regrows {value} at each of its next three actions.

entries.flavour: The old ones are heavier. Nobody has said why.

entries.name: Lich

design.fantasy: The lich, the Marsh's commander: a backliner of its own since 10 November, no rung of the revenant's line (Ryan: 'its no longer a revenant. It's its own thing ... a lich its own backliner to pair with it'); it stands behind the Draugr at tier three. Its sprite is still the Revenant's in another hue, a placeholder until it has art of its own. Its Dark Rite, a delayed heal on a countdown, is planned until the engine has a special with a countdown (Ryan, 28 October, mentioned a delayed heal; not built here).

entries.codex: The dead that commands the dead. It readies an ally to get back up once, and strikes from the back. Reach it, or purge what it readies.

actions.name: Soul Bolt
actions.text: A bolt of cold for {damage}.

actions.name: Reraise
actions.text: Readies one of its own, never itself: the next time it falls it gets back up, whole, once.

actions.name: Dark Rite
actions.text: A rite that lands two rounds on: every foe on its side regrows {value}.

entries.flavour: It does not fight. It makes sure the others do not stop.

design.niche: It hides behind the wall and keeps the wall standing. Reach it, or chew through.

entries.codex: Keeps to the back rank behind a wall of the dead and keeps the wall standing. Anything that can reach past the front is worth more here than anywhere else.

entries.name: Barrow Giant

design.fantasy: The Marsh's own massive line (Ryan, 30 October: "We also probably need more massive foes, yes?"; 31 October, agreeing Claude's lean): the genre's undead giant, risen from a barrow in rusted plate. The Marsh had no massive rank and file since the Bone Wyvern became an elite.
design.niche: Hard to keep down at its size: it knits its wounds over three actions, so burst it or purge the mending; its higher tiers ready themselves to get back up.
design.notes: Landed 31 October as a placeholder kit for Ryan's marks; every number a placeholder. Its art a rough placeholder (tools/placeholder_art.py), a reminder until a render is picked.

entries.codex: A giant that died in its armour and was buried in a barrow too small for it. It fills a whole column, and hurt, it knits itself back together over three rounds.

A wanderer since 3 November (Ryan: "Reaper might as well go full Persona and be a wanderer"): Persona's Reaper comes to any floor once you linger, so it walks out of any rift.
design.niche: It hunts the weakest machine, fast, and its Knell is a telegraphed knife two rounds out through the shield. A fight the detachment it catches cannot win, so the squad comes to it.
design.notes: Proposed 26 October; landed 30 October as a placeholder kit for Ryan's marks; to the wanderers 3 November, listed once under the Marsh and every domain's. Art picked and cut 18 October (art/foes/reaper).

entries.codex: It walks out of any rift, picks a machine and comes for it, faster than anything else on the field. Its scythe is bad; the knell is worse: a blow named two rounds ahead. Whatever it catches alone, it kills alone.

actions.name: Scythe
actions.text: The scythe, for {damage}.

actions.name: Death's Knell
actions.text: A bell rung for one machine: {damage}, two rounds on.

actions.name: Harvest
actions.text: A cut that rots: {damage}, and the entry it shows is corrupted.

entries.flavour: Gate order four, footnote: it is not that it has died. It is what died first.

entries.name: The Goblin Nob

design.fantasy: Slay the Spire's Gremlin Nob by archetype, the goblin line grown (Ryan, 3 November: "I like Nob a lot"; Nob was Warhammer's Ork rank before the Spire's gremlin borrowed it, and plain slang besides, so the word is free). Owned by what it punishes: the Spire's Nob punishes skills because skills are that game's defence; ours punishes the die and the heat.
design.niche: Its rage is its own from the fight's start: while it stands, every shield, vent or equipment entry the team spends makes its blows a point harder for the rest of the fight, shown on its chip as its attack climbs. Run hot or feed the Nob: reroll the shields into weapons, skip the vent, kill it fast; armour is no spend, so a plated machine answers it another way. Skull Bash scorches, so the weapons you lean on run hotter. The outs: the kill, a Suppress, a Purge, which lowers the rage it has gathered by its number.
design.notes: Landed 3 November as a placeholder kit on Ryan's marks (the Nob placed in the Meadow, alone, Claude's lean on his "wanderer or placed"; permanent rage, Claude's lean on his two shapes, so an elite's job is to make the player change plan, settled 4 November: "Nob permanent"); every number a placeholder. The rage was a Bellow, its opening move, until 8 November, when Ryan read that it had to cast it before it gained a stack: "It's not innate? ... That is so unbelievably incorrect"; the rage is its own from the start, and its kit two moves until a third is proposed. Its art a rough placeholder (tools/placeholder_art.py) until a render is picked. The Enraged status is the session's one new foe mechanism.
design.sprite: a goblin twice a goblin's size with a jutting jaw and small furious eyes, a crude iron plate strapped on one shoulder, a spiked club over the other, a string of trophies at its belt, drawn retro

entries.codex: A goblin grown big and angry. Every shield you raise, every vent you spend and every piece of equipment you use makes its club hit a point harder, for good. Its bash leaves you scorched. Kill it fast, or play through the heat.

actions.name: Rush
actions.text: A rush with the club, for {damage}.

actions.name: Skull Bash
actions.text: Skull Bash: {damage}, and the machine scorched.

entries.flavour: Gate order one, footnote: the big one gets angrier the more careful you are.

entries.name: The Bane

design.fantasy: Tolkien's Balrog by archetype, the shadow and flame on the mountain's bridge (Balrog is his coinage, so a name of ours: the Bane, for Durin's; Ryan, 3 November: "Balrog yes"). The Peak's hunter: it goes for the strongest, as it went for the wizard.
design.niche: Hunts the strongest machine, the fattest hull. Flame Whip burns, Shadow Blade comes through the shield, and below half Shadow and Flame scorches every machine. The tank is its prey, so the tank's heat is the question.
design.notes: Landed 3 November as a placeholder kit on Ryan's marks; every number a placeholder. Its art a rough placeholder (tools/placeholder_art.py) until a render is picked. Not winged: its wings are the shadow's, and the Fell Rider is the winged hunter.
design.sprite: a colossal demon of shadow and fire, a mane of flame over a body of black smoke and cinder, a whip of fire in one hand and a sword of flame in the other, horned, drawn retro

entries.codex: Shadow and flame, the size of a gate. It picks the strongest machine on the field and comes for it: a whip that leaves it ablating, a blade of shadow, and below half a fire that scorches everything. Keep the tank cool, or it is the first to go.

actions.name: Flame Whip
actions.text: The whip of flame: {damage}, and the machine Ablating ×2.

actions.name: Shadow Blade
actions.text: The blade of shadow, for {damage}.

actions.name: Shadow and Flame
actions.text: Shadow and flame: {damage} to every machine, each one scorched.

entries.flavour: Gate order seven: nothing passes the bridge. It was written for the other side.

entries.name: The Firelord

design.fantasy: Warcraft's Ragnaros by archetype, the Firelord of the Molten Core, the Magma Elemental line grown (Ryan, 3 November: placed). The register's own shape: the domain's wildlife grown with a pop-culture nod.
design.niche: The Hammer is a heavy blow that scorches. Submerge is a brace that names its follow-up: he sinks, two Sons of Flame (Salamanders) rise, and he surfaces, so the shelled round is a swarm's round. Area damage for the sons, burst for the lord.
design.notes: Landed 3 November as a placeholder kit on Ryan's marks; every number a placeholder. Sulfuras is Blizzard's coinage, so the move is the Hammer. Its art a rough placeholder (tools/placeholder_art.py) until a render is picked.
design.sprite: a colossal elemental of lava and black rock rising waist-deep from a pool of fire, a great hammer of slag raised in both hands, a crown of flame, drawn retro

entries.codex: The magma elementals' lord, waist-deep in its own fire. Its hammer scorches what it hits. When it sinks, its plate thickens for a round and two sons of flame come up beside it, then it surfaces: shield up for the sons, then back to the lord.

actions.name: The Hammer
actions.text: The hammer of slag: {damage}, and the machine scorched.

actions.name: Submerge
actions.text: It sinks into the fire: armour +{value} until its next action, and the Sons of Flame come next round.

actions.name: Sons of Flame
actions.text: Two sons of flame rise from the fire, into empty places at once, or into the pool when the line is full.

entries.flavour: Recruitment poster: THEY BROUGHT FIRE. Footnote: the fire brought a hammer.

entries.name: The Thunder Ape

design.fantasy: Monster Hunter's Rajang by archetype, the golden ape of the volcano whose fury is lightning (Capcom's coinage, so a name of ours; Ryan, 3 November: a ubiquitous entry and unique, since the roster has few lightning foes; placed). Careful: his favourite series.
design.niche: Hunts the strongest machine, fast, as it goes for the biggest threat. Lightning Beam switches off the entry its target shows, the engine's nearest thing to a shock; Rampage is the multi-punch, three strikes at half; Golden Rage is the mode (Ryan's read, 4 November): for three rounds its blows hit 2 harder under a point of plate, until a quarter of its HP is knocked out of it, when it staggers and loses its next action, or a Suppress breaks it; a Purge strips it. So the round it roars is the window: shield through the gold, or burst it. Enemy Shock, telegraphed, is the bible's open question, and this is the foe to carry it when it is settled.
design.notes: Landed 3 November as a placeholder kit on Ryan's marks; its kit by his read of 4 November: "the iconic moves are the spin, the multi-punch rampage, the lightning beam (which you have), and the cannonball dive. The golden rage is a mode, not an attack - it gets angry, transforms gaining power and armour, and transforms back after a time or getting staggered. It's a cycle that forces the player into a cycle of attack and defense, broken by a bold player with great timing. Not all of that translates into our game, but that's the read." Claude's translation: the mode a special (the golden effect: value its add, rounds its length, when calm so one rage at a time, weight 2 so it comes about a round in three while calm), the stagger the bold play's pay; Rampage the multi-punch; the beam kept; the Grab and Throw retired (a pin is Deviljho's). Left out of the three-move budget, for Ryan to swap in: the spin (a blow at every machine) and the cannonball dive (a breach from above). Every number a placeholder. Its art a rough placeholder (tools/placeholder_art.py) until a render is picked.
design.sprite: a hulking ape with a mane of black fur and two curling horns, lightning crackling between its fists and jaws, braced on its knuckles mid-charge, drawn retro

entries.codex: A horned ape that spits lightning. It picks the strongest machine on the field and goes for it: a beam that switches off the entry it shows, a rampage of three fists, and a roar that turns its fur gold. Gold, its blows hit harder and it wears a point of armour for three rounds, until a quarter of its HP is knocked out of it; then it staggers. Shield through the gold, or break it.

actions.name: Lightning Beam
actions.text: A beam of lightning: {damage}, and the entry it shows is switched off through its next turn.

actions.name: Rampage
actions.text: A rampage of fists: {damage}, three times.

actions.name: Golden Rage
actions.text: It roars and its fur goes gold: its blows hit 2 harder and it wears a point of armour for three rounds, until a quarter of its HP is knocked out of it; then it staggers.

entries.flavour: Field manual, appendix M: it is not a monkey. Do not call it a monkey.

entries.name: The Rust Monster

design.fantasy: Dungeons and Dragons' rust monster by archetype, the beast that eats metal, and our machines are metal (Ryan, 3 November: D&D a property to pull from; placed). The Waste's theft, grown teeth.
design.niche: It aims at a machine showing an intact weapon, the built aim. Its bite corrupts the entry shown; its antennae switch it off; when hurt it feeds and regrows. Redundancy on the die, the Waste's answer.
design.notes: Landed 3 November as a placeholder kit on Ryan's marks, in the Roc's place (dropped: soft); every number a placeholder. Its art a rough placeholder (tools/placeholder_art.py) until a render is picked.
design.sprite: a low insectile beast with a plated carapace the colour of rust, two long feathery antennae waving ahead of it, a paddle tail, skittering on four legs, drawn retro

entries.codex: It eats metal, and it can smell a loaded weapon. Its bite corrupts the entry a machine is showing, its antennae switch one off, and when it is hurt it feeds and grows back. Keep a second weapon on the die.

actions.name: Rusting Bite
actions.text: A bite that rusts: {damage}, and the entry it shows is corrupted.

actions.name: Antennae
actions.text: The antennae brush a machine: the entry it shows is switched off through its next turn.

actions.name: Feed
actions.text: It feeds on what it bit off: regrows {value} HP.

entries.flavour: Field manual, appendix K, amended: secure your weapons. Appendix N: from this too.

entries.name: The Skeleton King

design.fantasy: Diablo's Skeleton King, Leoric, by archetype, the crowned dead king who raises his court (the title is plain words; Ryan, 3 November: placed). The zombie-knight line grown, the Marsh's rising as a commander.
design.niche: Cleave is two strikes. Raise the Dead calls two Revenants; Rise readies one of his own to get back up once. Kill order and reach: the king before the court, or the court keeps coming back.
design.notes: Landed 3 November as a placeholder kit on Ryan's marks, in the Drowned King's place (dropped: soft); every number a placeholder. Its art a rough placeholder (tools/placeholder_art.py) until a render is picked. Drawn as a crowned skeleton on its feet with a mace, so it never steps on the Antiquarian's cloaked silhouette (Ryan's worry).
design.sprite: a tall skeleton king in rusted ornate plate and a tarnished crown, a great mace in both hands, a tattered royal cloak, standing over a kneeling revenant, drawn retro

entries.codex: A dead king with a crown and a mace, and his court comes when he calls. He cleaves twice, raises revenants from the mud, and readies his knights to get back up. Kill him before the court, or the court never stays down.

actions.name: Cleave
actions.text: The mace, twice: {damage} each.

actions.name: Raise the Dead
actions.text: Two revenants rise from the mud, into empty places at once, or into the pool when the line is full.

actions.name: Rise
actions.text: Rise: one of its own is readied to get back up once when it falls.

entries.flavour: Gate order four, appendix: the crown does not make it alive. It makes the others listen.

entries.name: The Fell Rider

design.fantasy: Tolkien's Nazgûl on the fell beast by archetype (his coinages, so a name of ours; Ryan, 3 November: "Nazgul is good", the mount his to settle: the fell beast is Claude's lean, winged, so the Marsh has a hunter that crosses the walls the team holds; the horse at tier one would be a second entry with the same kit, and neither mount the Witch-king at the gate, a blitz rather than a hunt). The Marsh's hunter now the Reaper wanders. The Black Rider was its working name until it met Megami Tensei's Fiend of that name.
design.niche: Winged, it crosses walls and water, and it hunts the strongest machine, the bearer. Its blade corrupts the entry shown, its shriek costs the team a reroll, and below half the Black Breath lands on every machine. A wall is no answer to it; the kill is.
design.notes: Landed 3 November as a placeholder kit on Ryan's marks; every number a placeholder. Its art a rough placeholder (tools/placeholder_art.py) until a render is picked. The mount settled 4 November (Ryan): the fell beast at every tier, since flying is its map identity, no horse at the lower tiers, and no Witch-king, whose silhouette is the Skeleton King's.
design.sprite: a black-cloaked rider with no face in its hood astride a vast leathery winged beast with a long neck and a toothed maw, a long pale blade in its hand, drawn retro

entries.codex: A rider with no face on a beast with wings. Walls and water are nothing to it, and it comes for the strongest machine on the field: a blade that corrupts the entry it shows, a shriek that takes a reroll from the team, and below half a breath that reaches everything. There is no hiding from it; kill it.

actions.name: Fell Blade
actions.text: A pale blade: {damage}, and the entry it shows is corrupted.

actions.name: Shriek
actions.text: A shriek that stops the heart: the team has {value} fewer reroll next round.

actions.name: Black Breath
actions.text: The Black Breath: {damage} to every machine.

entries.flavour: Gate order four, footnote: it did not come over the wall. It came over the wall's wall.

entries.name: The Antiquarian

design.fantasy: Darkest Dungeon's Collector by archetype, the cloaked thing with a cage for a head that turns up in any hall and collects the heads of the fallen (Ryan, 3 November: placed or wandering, either; placed in the Marsh, the dungeon, Claude's lean, so the Shuffler wanders alone). The Antiquarian since 4 November, Ryan's name: Darkest Dungeon's Antiquarian is its hero who collects trinkets, so the name is a double reference the plain word carries straight, an antiquarian being a collector of old things (Claude's read: not too much, since a player who knows neither reads a collector of antiquities with a cage for a head; the id antiquarian since 9 November). A modern roguelike's homage, made retro.
design.niche: Collect calls what it has gathered, three Revenants; Reach comes through the shield; below half it collects the living, a blow at every machine that corrupts. Kill order: the Collector before it fills the line.
design.notes: Landed 3 November as a placeholder kit on Ryan's marks; every number a placeholder. Its art a rough placeholder (tools/placeholder_art.py) until a render is picked. Drawn cloaked and faceless with a lantern cage for a head, so it never steps on the Skeleton King's crowned silhouette (Ryan's worry).
design.sprite: a tall gaunt figure in a long dark cloak whose head is an iron lantern cage with a pale light inside, a staff in one hand and three severed heads hung from its belt, drawn retro

entries.codex: Tall, cloaked, and its head is a cage with a light in it. It comes with the heads it has collected, and it collects more: three dead rise when it calls, its reach is long, and below half it reaches for everything at once. Kill it before the line fills, or join the collection.

actions.name: Collect
actions.text: The collected rise: three revenants, into empty places at once, or into the pool when the line is full.

actions.name: Reach
actions.text: A long cold hand: {damage}.

actions.name: Collect the Living
actions.text: It reaches for everything: {damage} to every machine, and the entry each shows is corrupted.

entries.flavour: Gate order four, appendix: it is not collecting for anyone. That is the worst part.

entries.name: The World Eater

design.fantasy: Monster Hunter's Deviljho by archetype, the invader that barges into any hunt and fights whoever is there (Capcom's coinage, so a name of ours; Ryan, 3 November: "Jho (wanderer)", the original invader to a true fan; 4 November, its in-world epithets as the name: "World Eater, The Endless Hunger, The Great Devourer, and the Pickle", the World Eater Claude's pick, the Pickle the fans' joke, which the register plays straight; the id world_eater since 9 November). The roster's second saurian after the Obsidian Tyrant, kept apart by its kit. Careful: his favourite series.
design.niche: It pushes for the gate at speed and tramples whatever it meets. Chomp; Dragon Breath, a blow at every machine that corrupts the entry shown, dragonblight's own effect, the element knocked off your weapon; below half the Pin, a blow that leaves the machine Crushed, Defense Down by archetype: every blow it takes through the next round lands two harder, so the pack's blows after the pin and the next turn's bite. Its hunger has no clean piece yet: merge is the King Gel's and it comes alone.
design.notes: Landed 3 November as a placeholder kit on Ryan's marks; every number a placeholder. Its art a rough placeholder (tools/placeholder_art.py) until a render is picked. Ryan, 4 November: "I would probably rework the below half attack into a form of its pin, since that inflicts Defense Down in game, something we don't have." So Savage Bite is the Pin: a blow, and the crush rider lays Crushed (a point more on every blow the machine takes a stack, through the next round, Flak's shape on the other body); a Ward turns it away, an ally's Cleanse lifts it, a shield takes the extra first. The forms not taken: its armour counting for nothing through the round (nothing on a car) and its shield halved (fiddly at single digits).
design.sprite: a huge hunched saurian with a massive jaw of crooked teeth, spines down its back, a thick tail, scars all over its dark green hide, stamping forward with its head low, drawn retro

entries.codex: It walks out of any rift hungry, and it goes for the gate at a run. Its bite is bad; its breath is worse, a blow at every machine that corrupts the entry it shows. Below half it pins: a blow, and every blow that machine takes through the next round lands two harder. Cleanse the pinned, or shield it, and get in its way with everything.

actions.name: Chomp
actions.text: The jaws, for {damage}.

actions.name: Dragon Breath
actions.text: Dragon breath over every machine: {damage} each, and the entry each shows is corrupted.

actions.name: Pin
actions.text: It pins: {damage}, and every blow the machine takes through the next round lands 2 harder.

entries.flavour: Field manual, appendix M: if it is in your hunt, it is your hunt now.

entries.name: Rider of the Wild Hunt

design.fantasy: The Wild Hunt, the riders of European folklore that cross the winter sky and take whoever they catch, the Witcher's take the homage (riders in spiked plate on gaunt horses, frost in their wake; the name is folklore's, so it stays). Ryan, 3 November: "Wild Hunt is better, and this is a good place to make an elite pack of multiple clones instead of a unique unit", a wanderer: the Hunt rides between worlds, so it rides out of any rift.
design.niche: Three riders, winged, hunting the slowest machine, the one that cannot outrun the Hunt. Each lance is a point harder for every other rider standing, the engine's swarm, so the pack is the threat and thinning it is the answer; Frost switches off the entry its target shows.
design.notes: Landed 3 November as a placeholder kit on Ryan's marks, the first elite composition led by a foe at a strength above one; every number a placeholder. Its art a rough placeholder (tools/placeholder_art.py) until a render is picked.
design.sprite: a gaunt rider in black spiked plate with a horned helm astride a skeletal horse wreathed in frost, a long lance couched, riding on the air, drawn retro

entries.codex: They ride in threes across the sky and take the slowest. Each lance hits harder for every other rider still up, and their frost switches off whatever a machine is showing. Thin them, and the Hunt is only a rider.

actions.name: Lance
actions.text: A lance from the Hunt for {damage}: more for every other rider standing.

actions.name: Frost
actions.text: Frost in its wake: {damage}, and the entry it shows is switched off through its next turn.

entries.flavour: Gate order four, footnote: they are not from the Marsh. They are not from anywhere.

entries.name: The Shuffler

design.fantasy: Darkest Dungeon's Shambler by archetype, the thing that comes when the light is out, in any hall (Ryan, 3 November: "Shambler should be on the table"). The Shuffler since 4 November, Ryan's name, which winks at its game's shuffle of the party too; the id shuffler since 9 November. A wanderer: a Fracture is its dark, so it walks out of any rift.
design.niche: Every other move spawns two Shuffler Spawn, so the fight fills while it stands; Dark Caress corrupts; below half it fractures, a blow at every machine. The sudden swarm the elites' definition named. Its shuffle of the party has no analogue, since machines hold no rank, so the spawn is its curveball.
design.notes: Landed 3 November as a placeholder kit on Ryan's marks; every number a placeholder. Its art a rough placeholder (tools/placeholder_art.py) until a render is picked.
design.sprite: a shapeless mass of dark flesh and eyes dragging itself forward on a dozen tentacles, pale growths budding from its sides, drawn retro

entries.codex: A shapeless thing that comes in the dark. It buds: two spawn every time it chooses to, into any empty place. Its caress corrupts the entry a machine shows, and below half it comes apart at everything. Kill it before the line is all spawn.

actions.name: Dark Caress
actions.text: A dark caress: {damage}, and the entry it shows is corrupted.

actions.name: Spawn
actions.text: It buds: two Shuffler Spawn, into empty places at once, or into the pool when the line is full.

actions.name: Fracture
actions.text: It comes apart: {damage} to every machine.

entries.flavour: Gate order four, last line, written in a different hand: do not let the lights go out.

entries.name: Shuffler Spawn

design.fantasy: The Shuffler's buds, Darkest Dungeon's Shambler's Spawn by archetype: small, many, and worse together (named with their parent, 4 November).
design.niche: A lash that swarms: a point more for every other spawn standing. Area damage, the Meadow's answer in the Marsh.

entries.codex: A bud off the Shuffler, with teeth. Each one lashes harder for every other one standing.

actions.name: Lash
actions.text: A lash for {damage}: more for every other spawn standing.

entries.flavour: Gate order four, footnote: count them again.

entries.name: Enkidu

design.fantasy: Gilgamesh's companion, the wild man of the epic and the beast at the rival's side in Final Fantasy V (a myth's name, so it stays; 3 November, a cheap add: a composition's members may differ by tier). Joins Gilgamesh at tier three.
design.niche: Stands behind Gilgamesh: a claw, a mend on the most hurt of its own, a roar that rallies the pack. Kill order: the beast behind the swordsman, or the swordsman never goes down.

entries.codex: Gilgamesh's beast, and it minds him. It mends him when he is hurt and roars him on; kill it first, or the fight with him never ends.

actions.name: Claw
actions.text: A claw, for {damage}.

actions.name: Mend
actions.text: It licks the wound: the most hurt of its own regrows {value} HP.

actions.name: Roar
actions.text: A roar: every other foe on the field hits {value} harder, fading by half each round.

entries.flavour: Field manual, appendix L, amended: he brought a friend.

entries.name: Rotbloom

design.fantasy: The genre's Malboro by archetype (Final Fantasy's coinage, so a name of ours; Rotbloom is a working name): a bloated maw-plant whose breath carries every ailment at once. It stays beside Floraison (Ryan, 24 October: mechanically very different, and a different silhouette). To the rank and file 3 November (Ryan: the Malboro is a species, no named entity, and "could be a rank and file"; tier two and up): the Meadow's massive at tiers two and three, its bed a formation, Bad Breath the twist.
design.niche: Bad Breath lays everything at once on every machine: Burning, Scorched, a switched-off entry and a corrupted one. Cleanse is the answer and a Ward the prevention; below half it seeds the ground with mandragoras, the Meadow's numbers.
design.notes: Landed 30 October as a boss, a runnable placeholder kit for Ryan's marks (the slate, docs/bosses_proposal.md); a massive rank and file since 3 November, its escorts retired and its bed a formation at tiers two and three; every number a placeholder. Its art a rough placeholder (tools/placeholder_art.py) until a render is picked (design.sprite is the forge's brief).
design.sprite: a colossal bloated plant creature squatting on a mass of thick roots, a huge round maw ringed with dripping fangs gaping in its swollen body, a mass of writhing tendrils bursting from its sides, sickly green and yellow-brown blotched hide, a foul cloud seeping from its mouth

a colossal swollen bulb of a plant monster with no eyes, its whole front a wide fanged mouth, a crown of thick tendrils lashing forward, its hide a mottled sickly green with weeping yellow sores, a haze of spores around it

a colossal rotting flower monster rearing up on a knot of roots, its petals peeled back from a round mouth of needle teeth, dozens of tendrils hanging from it like a beard, dull green and brown, a foul mist pouring out between its teeth

a colossal squat plant beast like a giant gourd with a mouth, tendrils coiled round it and reaching out on every side, its sickly green skin stretched tight and blotched brown, a dripping fanged mouth breathing out a cloud of rot

entries.codex: A walking bloom of rot. Its breath carries everything at once: every machine it reaches is left ablating, runs hot, loses the entry it is showing and has it corrupted. Cleanse what it lays; a Ward keeps it off. Hurt badly, it seeds the ground.

actions.name: Tendrils
actions.text: Tendrils, twice: {damage} each.

actions.name: Bad Breath
actions.text: Bad Breath over every machine: {damage} each, and each one Ablating, scorched, the entry it shows switched off and corrupted.

actions.name: Seedfall
actions.text: Below half, it seeds the ground: two mandragoras join the fight.

entries.flavour: Gate order one, amended again: if it is green and it smells like that, masks on.

entries.name: Floraison

design.fantasy: Clair Obscur's Bourgeon by archetype, under Ryan's name (15 October: the flowering): a humanoid plant whose head is a flower's maw. The game places one in its Meadows. Art picked 26 October (the paint-out of the maw's eyes).
design.niche: It takes a machine out of the fight: the swallow holds one machine for two rounds, until Floraison falls or until it has lost a quarter of its HP since, so the team fights a man down, answered before it lands by a Ward, a Lure, a Suppress or a Disrupt and after it by focus on Floraison. Its combos are many small strikes, which plate shrugs off: lure them onto the tank.
design.notes: Landed 30 October as a runnable placeholder kit for Ryan's marks (the slate, docs/bosses_proposal.md); every number a placeholder. The swallow and the combos are Ryan's (15 October); two rounds, never the last machine able to act, and no damage while held are Claude's placeholders. The release at a quarter of its HP lost since the swallow, Ryan's 31 October (agreeing Claude's lean on his Clair Obscur stagger); a lost action on top, the stagger's bigger form, waits on the plain release reading weak.
design.sprite: a colossal humanoid plant creature standing upright on two thick root-legs, its body knotted vines and green bark, two long vine arms ending in thorned claws, its head a great flower bud whose peeled-back pink-and-green petals ring a round mouth rimmed with thorns and full of needle teeth

entries.name: The Astromancer

design.fantasy: Golden Sun: The Lost Age's Star Magician by archetype, the Treasure Isle superboss behind its four kinds of Ball (Camelot's coinages, so names of ours: an astromancer is a star-mage, and its orbs are warding, storm, mending and fuming), on Ryan's go of 4 November ("If you think another golden sun works as a boss or elite, feel free to throw it in"); to its fans "one of the most challenging, thought-provoking, and tricky encounters" in the series, since the whole fight is which ball to kill first. A wanderer, since its cave is no domain's.
design.niche: The kill-order elite. The Warding Orb is a part: while it stands the Astromancer is Guarded (the Guardian Ball's aura), and it grows back three rounds after it falls (the resummon). The Mending Orb cures the most hurt of them; the Storm Orb's lightning switches off the entry shown and its Shine reaches every machine; Mystic Call brings two Fuming Orbs, which burst on a machine through the shield. So the question each round: the mender first, the ward to open the mage, the fuming orbs before they burst, the storm last; the Star Magician's own priority puzzle. The first elite in parts; one Warding Orb since the parts system guards by all of them.

entries.name: Storm Orb

design.fantasy: The Star Magician's Thunder Ball by archetype, the Jupiter caster among its orbs, the least durable and the one the guides leave for last.

entries.name: Mending Orb

design.fantasy: The Star Magician's Refresh Ball by archetype, the healer that plies its master back to full; the first thing a guide tells you to kill.
design.niche: Earnest Ply cures the most hurt of its own; a soft blow otherwise. First in the kill order: reach to the healer, the Marsh's question asked by a wanderer.
design.notes: Landed 4 November; a placeholder kit, every number a placeholder. Its art a rough placeholder (tools/placeholder_art.py).
design.sprite: a green orb with a slow pulse of light at its heart, drawn retro

actions.name: Glimmer
actions.text: A glimmer: {damage}.

entries.name: Fuming Orb

design.fantasy: The Star Magician's Anger Ball by archetype, the red one that self-destructs for heavy damage, the one its guides say to kill first; here the mage's summon, two a call.
design.niche: A fuse: Fume is a blow, and Burst a self-destruct through the shield, announced like any move. Kill it before it bursts, or shield what it picked.
design.notes: Landed 4 November; a placeholder kit, every number a placeholder. Its art a rough placeholder (tools/placeholder_art.py).

actions.name: Fume

actions.name: Burst
actions.text: It bursts for {damage}, and is gone.

entries.name: King Gel

design.fantasy: Dragon Quest's King Slime by archetype, the slime that wears the crown (the genre's coinage, so the King Gel, by our Gel; Ryan, 15 October: a mark, and yes to the slate's last five, 30 October).
design.niche: It stands with Gels round it, and Merge takes every Gel and half on the field into itself, regrowing what they had left and hitting harder for each: kill order against a heal, the Meadow's numbers poured into one body. Thin the Gels first, or stop the merge; once its court is gone it only slams.
design.notes: Landed 30 October as a runnable placeholder kit (Ryan: "Yes to all waiting bosses"); every number a placeholder. Its art a rough placeholder (tools/placeholder_art.py), a reminder until a render is picked. Its escort is its own (an escort composition that names it), Gels at every tier, so its merge has something to take in.

variants: an enormous round blue gel slime wearing a small golden jewelled crown, a wide toothless grin, two smaller gels clinging to its sides like courtiers

entries.codex: The Gels' king, and it eats its own. It calls every Gel on the field into itself, healing what they had left and hitting harder for each one, so kill the Gels before it does. Below half it simply falls on everything.

actions.name: Body Slam
actions.text: Its whole weight, for {damage}.

actions.text: Every Gel on the field is taken in: it regrows the HP they had left, and its next move hits {value} harder for each.

actions.name: Belly Flop
actions.text: It falls on everything: {damage} to every machine.

entries.flavour: Field manual, appendix K: the big one is not a different species. It is all the small ones you missed.

entries.name: The Pilgrim

design.fantasy: Final Fantasy's Tonberry by archetype, the little lantern-bearer everyone dreads (the series' coinage, so a name of ours: the Pilgrim, for its slow walk with the lantern; Ryan, 15 October: the Tonberry everyone hates). Keep the dread, drop the unfairness: the countdown shown is the fairness. To the elites 3 November (Ryan: "Tonberry is an obvious elite"): the Waste's hunter he marked on 24 October, walking a hex a turn after the nearest machine, the Tonberry's own joke, slow and sure.
design.niche: It hunts the nearest machine at a walk, so the map can outrun it for a while and the meter cannot. Its knife comes on a countdown of two, through the shield, so the team sees it walking; below half, Karma, a point heavier for every foe the team has killed this fight, through the shield. Kill order turns over: the Pilgrim before its needlers, or the grudge grows with every kill.
design.notes: Landed 30 October as a boss, a runnable placeholder kit (Ryan: "Yes to all waiting bosses"); an elite since 3 November, its escorts retired and three Needlers its wake at every tier so Karma has fuel; every number a placeholder. Its art a rough placeholder (tools/placeholder_art.py), a reminder until a render is picked. The move names, Chef's Knife and Karma, are the genre's plain words, for Ryan's name pass.
design.sprite: a small hunched green creature in a brown hooded monk's robe shuffling forward, a lit lantern held out in one hand and a long kitchen knife in the other, its yellow eyes glinting under the hood
variants: a small hunched green creature in a brown hooded monk's robe shuffling forward, a lit lantern held out in one hand and a long kitchen knife in the other, its yellow eyes glinting under the hood

entries.codex: Small, slow and patient. It picks the nearest machine and walks toward it with a lantern and a knife, and you will see the knife coming two rounds out. Below half it remembers every one of its own you have killed, and the blow grows with them: kill it first, or leave its needlers be.

actions.text: A swing of the lantern, for {damage}.

actions.name: Chef's Knife
actions.text: It walks closer: in two rounds the knife, {damage}.

actions.name: Karma
actions.text: Karma: {damage}, a point for every foe you have killed this fight.

entries.name: The Djinn

design.fantasy: The desert's own spirit, the genie by archetype (the jinn are the Thousand and One Nights' and older, a myth's word, so it stays). The Waste's third boss for a day (31 October), then the rank and file (Ryan, 2 November: "Djinn can be a rank-and-file since its a trope archetype. Could be backline, frontline, or massive, depending on the slant"); Claude's slant the back-rank caster, the Waste's first purge in the ranks (section 12's carrier question), since the slate's kit was built to carry it.
design.niche: The Waste's purge in the ranks: it unmakes what a machine's die bought, every buff a face granted, on the machine carrying the most, and hurt it slips into a mirage, a Barrier that eats the next weapon blow. A back-rank caster: reach it, spend a buff before it is unmade, or put the buff on the machine it is not aiming at.
design.notes: A rank-and-file caster since 2 November, at tier two's numbers; every number a placeholder. Its art a rough placeholder (tools/placeholder_art.py), a reminder until a render is picked. A tier-three recolour of it (an Efreet, the fire jinn) is a cheap add on Ryan's mark.
design.sprite: a towering blue genie with a muscular bare torso and gold armbands, a turban set with a red gem, its lower body a tapering swirl of desert smoke, a curved scimitar raised in one hand
variants: a towering blue genie with a muscular bare torso and gold armbands, a turban set with a red gem, its lower body a tapering swirl of desert smoke, a curved scimitar raised in one hand

entries.codex: A spirit of the deep desert, bound to no lamp. Its blade is plain; its wishing is not: it unmakes what a machine's die bought, and hurt, it hides behind a mirage that eats the next blow. Reach it, pop the mirage cheaply, and spend a buff before it unmakes it.

actions.name: Scimitar
actions.text: A curved blade of smoke, for {damage}.

actions.name: Unmake
actions.text: It unmakes a wish: the machine carrying the most buffs loses every buff an entry's spend bought.

actions.name: Mirage
actions.text: It slips into a mirage: the next weapon blow on it deals nothing.

entries.flavour: Field manual, appendix K: do not make a wish. Do not ask what it meant by that.

entries.name: The Ruby Colossus

design.fantasy: Final Fantasy VII's Ruby Weapon by archetype (WEAPON is the series' coinage, so a name of ours; the Ruby Colossus a working name): the red colossus buried in the desert round the Gold Saucer, its tentacles in the sand, whose Whirlsand blew a party member out of the fight. The Waste's third boss since 2 November (Ryan: "Ruby weapon is cool"), in the Djinn's place.
design.niche: A boss in parts with no guard: its two tentacles hit on their own, one through the shield and one twice, and grow back three rounds after they fall, so every die is a choice between the arms and the body. Whirlsand buries a machine (a swallow: two rounds, until the Colossus falls, or until it has lost a quarter of its HP since). Below half, Ultima gathers for three rounds and lands on every machine. Dig the machine out by focus on the body, kill the breaching arm or eat its blows, and shield everything for Ultima.
design.notes: Landed 2 November as a runnable placeholder kit for Ryan's marks; every number a placeholder. Its tentacles' blows of 6 and 4 and a regrowth of two rounds walled the stock teams alone at tiers two and three (docs/measurements.md, 2 November): 4, 3 and three rounds since, on the what-if. Its art a rough placeholder (tools/placeholder_art.py), a reminder until a render is picked. Its escort a Basilisk and a Pit Antlion at tier two, Gorgons, the Antlion Queen and a Pit Antlion at tier three: stone and pits beside a buried machine, so the tempo it takes is pressed.

Its two tentacles strike on their own and grow back when cut; its Whirlsand buries a machine until it falls or is bled a quarter of its HP; below half it gathers Ultima, three rounds to shield for. The arms or the body: every die chooses.

entries.name: Thrashing Tentacle

design.fantasy: One of the Ruby Colossus's two tentacles, a part of a boss in parts with no guard (the slate's Ruby Weapon homage): the one that thrashes.
design.niche: A part that strikes twice, each strike paying armour: plate shrugs it, paper does not. It grows back three rounds on.

entries.name: The Phantom Train

design.fantasy: Final Fantasy VI's Phantom Train by archetype, the ghost train that carries the dead (the old stories' ghost train, so the name stays). Yes to the slate's last five, 30 October.
design.niche: It runs down what stands in front of it, and its whistle calls two Ghosts up to ride, summoners calling summoners while it stands; below half it builds steam for a round and runs over every machine. The passengers or the engine: kill order and burst.
design.notes: Landed 30 October as a runnable placeholder kit (Ryan: "Yes to all waiting bosses"); every number a placeholder. Its art a rough placeholder (tools/placeholder_art.py), a reminder until a render is picked.

variants: a black steam locomotive bursting out of fog, a grinning skull-like face on its smokebox, ghostly green fire in its firebox, pale spirits trailing from its funnel

actions.name: Whistle
actions.text: The whistle: two Ghosts come up to ride.

actions.name: Last Run
actions.text: It builds steam: next round, {damage} to every machine.

entries.name: The Vampire Lord

design.fantasy: Suikoden's Neclord by archetype, the vampire lord who will not stay dead (Suikoden's coinage, so a name of ours, the genre's own words). Yes to the slate's last five, 30 October.
design.niche: Hard to keep down, the Marsh's own: its bite heals what it takes from the hull, it readies itself once a fight to get back up whole, and below half it drinks from every machine. Shield what it bites (a shield starves the drain), burn it (Burning takes back what it drains), stop the readying (a Suppress, a Disrupt, a Purge on its Getting Back Up), and burst it twice if it rises.
design.notes: Landed 30 October as a runnable placeholder kit (Ryan: "Yes to all waiting bosses"); every number a placeholder. Its art a rough placeholder (tools/placeholder_art.py), a reminder until a render is picked. At 40 HP, under the slate's 48, since it may rise once whole. Its drain takes from the hull alone: one of shield and hull walled Wainwright & Sutler's trio at every HP tried down to 24 (0 to 10% won), the shield doing nothing against the heal; hull only, every row won it at 40 (30 October, docs/measurements.md).

actions.text: It readies itself: when it falls it gets back up once, whole.

entries.name: The Obsidian Tyrant

design.notes: Landed 30 October as a runnable placeholder kit (Ryan: "Yes to all waiting bosses"); every number a placeholder. Its art a rough placeholder (tools/placeholder_art.py), a reminder until a render is picked. Its countdown opens on a condition that reads a fallen part (part_fallen), built for it.

actions.name: Firestorm

actions.name: Goad

design.fantasy: Clair Obscur's Sciel by archetype (Ryan, 16 October): the reader of fate who marks a foe and collects later, her twin-bladed scythe her defining feature (a staff with a reaping blade at each end, spun and thrown). Ryan's name, 16 October: the Augur read omens for Rome. Her look is ours: a laced leather vest, shirt, trousers and boots, bare-headed, the bone charms, the long crescent blades (Ryan's notes of 18 October over three rounds, each asking for less cloth and bigger blades; the hero style prompt's robes and flowing cloth, and this text's own words for what she must not wear, were what kept drawing them, so her renders take a prompt of their own that names only what she wears).

Her omen is the countdown: named at one machine as the round opens, it lands two rounds on, so the warning is the whole fight (shield that machine, Suppress or Disrupt her, or reach her first). Below half every omen comes due at once, on every machine, the next round: the countdown and the every-machine blow on one move.

design.fantasy: The one who calls something bigger: Final Fantasy's summoner, Golden Sun's adepts, the demon summoners of Megami Tensei. Its summons answer the deep violet circle, appear for one move, and go. Its own power shows as deep violet rune circles in its palms, never fire (the Black Mage's) and never the rock (the Elemental's): Ryan, 13 October; the fire and the ice are the summons'.
design.niche: On its own it is a mage with a weak blow; its summons are the fight, each a move rather than a companion (three massive companions could not stand in two ranks of four, and the Tamer and the Necromancer already call foes into the fight every round). Skaði's frost corrupts the component every machine shows; Surtr's fire scorches every machine once it is hurt. The answer is the back rank: reach it, Suppress it or Disrupt it.
